questions.q: If \(y^2=P(x)\), a polynomial of degree \(3\), then \(2\dfrac d{dx}\left(y^3\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)\) equals
questions.sol: \(2yy'=P'\) and differentiating again, \(2yy''+2y'^2=P''\). So \(y^3y''=\dfrac{y^2P''}2-(yy')^2=\dfrac{2PP''-P'^2}4\), whose derivative is \(\dfrac{PP'''}2\).

questions.q: The order of the differential equation whose general solution given by \(y=(c_1+c_2)\cos(x+c_3)-c_4e^{x+c_5}\), where \(c_1,c_2,c_3,c_4,c_5\) are arbitrary constants, is
questions.sol: \(y=A\cos(x+c_3)-Be^x\) with \(A=c_1+c_2\), \(B=c_4e^{c_5}\): only three independent constants.

questions.q: A solution of the differential equation \(\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2-x\dfrac{dy}{dx}+y=0\) is
If \(x^2+y^2=1\), then
questions.sol: Differentiating twice: \(x+yy'=0\), then \(1+(y')^2+yy''=0\).

questions.q: If \(y(t)\) is a solution of \((1+t)\dfrac{dy}{dt}-ty=1\) and \(y(0)=-1\), then \(y(1)\) is equal to
questions.sol: Integrating factor \((1+t)e^{-t}\): \(y(1+t)e^{-t}=-e^{-t}+C\), and \(y(0)=-1\) gives \(C=0\). So \(y=-\dfrac1{1+t}\).

questions.q: If \(y=y(x)\) and \(\dfrac{2+\sin x}{y+1}\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)=-\cos x\), \(y(0)=1\), then \(y\left(\dfrac\pi2\right)\) equals
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{dy}{y+1}=-\dfrac{\cos x\,dx}{2+\sin x}\) gives \((y+1)(2+\sin x)=C=4\). At \(x=\dfrac\pi2\): \(y+1=\dfrac43\).

questions.q: The solution of primitive equation \((x^2+y^2)dy=xy\,dx\), is \(y=y(x)\). If \(y(1)=1\) and \(y(x_0)=e\), then \(x_0\) is
questions.sol: With \(x=vy\): \(\dfrac{dx}{dy}=v+\dfrac1v\) gives \(v\,dv=\dfrac{dy}y\), so \(\dfrac{x^2}{2y^2}=\ln y+\dfrac12\). At \(y=e\): \(x^2=3e^2\).

questions.q: For the primitive integral equation \(y\,dx+y^2dy=x\,dy\); \(x\in R\), \(y>0\), \(y=y(x)\), \(y(1)=1\), then \(y(-3)\) is
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{y\,dx-x\,dy}{y^2}=-dy\), i.e. \(d\left(\dfrac xy\right)=-dy\): \(\dfrac xy=-y+2\). At \(x=-3\): \(y^2-2y-3=0\), \(y=3\).

questions.q: The differential equation \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{\sqrt{1-y^2}}y\) determines a family of circles with
opts: variable radii and a fixed centre at \((0,1)\)
variable radii and fixed centre at \((0,-1)\)
fixed radius \(1\) and variable centres along the \(x\)-axis
fixed radius \(1\) and variable centres along the \(y\)-axis.

questions.q: A curve passes through the point \(\left(1,\dfrac\pi6\right)\). Let the slope of the curve at each point \((x,y)\) be \(\dfrac yx+\sec\left(\dfrac yx\right)\), \(x>0\). Then the equation of the curve is
questions.sol: With \(y=vx\): \(x\dfrac{dv}{dx}=\sec v\), so \(\sin v=\log x+c\); at \(\left(1,\frac\pi6\right)\): \(c=\dfrac12\).

questions.q: The function \(y=f(x)\) is the solution of the differential equation \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{xy}{x^2-1}=\dfrac{x^4+2x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\) in \((-1,1)\) satisfying \(f(0)=0\). Then \(\displaystyle\int_{-\sqrt3/2}^{\sqrt3/2}f(x)dx\) is
questions.sol: Integrating factor \(\sqrt{1-x^2}\): \(y\sqrt{1-x^2}=\dfrac{x^5}5+x^2\). The odd part integrates to \(0\): \(2\displaystyle\int_0^{\sqrt3/2}\dfrac{x^2}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}dx=\left[\sin^{-1}x-x\sqrt{1-x^2}\right]_0^{\sqrt3/2}=\dfrac\pi3-\dfrac{\sqrt3}4\).

questions.q: If \(y=y(x)\) satisfies the differential equation \(8\sqrt x\left(\sqrt{9+\sqrt x}\right)dy=\left(\sqrt{4+\sqrt{9+\sqrt x}}\right)^{-1}dx\), \(x>0\) and \(y(0)=\sqrt7\), then \(y(256)=\)
questions.sol: With \(u=\sqrt{4+\sqrt{9+\sqrt x}}\): \(du=\dfrac{dx}{8u\sqrt{9+\sqrt x}\sqrt x}=dy\). So \(y=u+c\), and \(y(0)=\sqrt7\) gives \(c=0\). \(y(256)=\sqrt{4+\sqrt{25}}=3\).

questions.q: Let \(f:[1,\infty)\to\mathbb R\) be a differentiable function such that \(f(1)=\dfrac13\) and \(3\displaystyle\int_1^xf(t)dt=xf(x)-\dfrac{x^3}3\), \(x\in[1,\infty)\). Let \(e\) denote the base of the natural logarithm. Then the value of \(f(e)\) is
questions.sol: Differentiating: \(3f=f+xf'-x^2\), i.e. \(\left(\dfrac f{x^2}\right)'=\dfrac1x\). So \(f=x^2\left(\ln x+\dfrac13\right)\).

questions.q: Let \(f(x)\) be a continuously differentiable function on the interval \((0,\infty)\) such that \(f(1)=2\) and \(\lim\limits_{t\to x}\dfrac{t^{10}f(x)-x^{10}f(t)}{t^9-x^9}=1\) for each \(x>0\). Then, for all \(x>0\), \(f(x)\) is equal to
questions.sol: By L'Hôpital's rule (in \(t\)): \(\dfrac{10x^9f(x)-x^{10}f'(x)}{9x^8}=1\), i.e. \(\left(\dfrac f{x^{10}}\right)'=-\dfrac9{x^{12}}\). So \(f=\dfrac9{11x}+cx^{10}\) and \(f(1)=2\) gives \(c=\dfrac{13}{11}\).

questions.q: The differential equation representing the family of curves \(y^2=2c\left(x+\sqrt c\right)\), where \(c\) is a positive parameter, is of
questions.sol: \(2yy'=2c\) gives \(c=yy'\). Substituting: \(y-2xy'=2y'\sqrt{yy'}\); squaring: \((y-2xy')^2=4y(y')^3\) — first order, third degree.

questions.q: A curve \(y=f(x)\) passes through \((1,1)\) and tangent at \(P(x,y)\) cuts the \(x\)-axis and \(y\) axis at \(A\) and \(B\) respectively such that \(BP:AP=3:1\), then
questions.sol: \(A=\left(x-\dfrac y{y'},0\right)\) and \(P=\dfrac{3A+B}4\): \(x=\dfrac34\left(x-\dfrac y{y'}\right)\), so \(xy'+3y=0\) and \(y=\dfrac1{x^3}\). The normal at \((1,1)\) has slope \(\dfrac13\): \(x-3y+2=0\).

questions.q: If \(y(x)\) satisfies the differential equation \(y'-y\tan x=2x\sec x\) and \(y(0)=0\), then
questions.sol: \((y\cos x)'=2x\) gives \(y=x^2\sec x\) and \(y'=2x\sec x+x^2\sec x\tan x\). \(y\left(\frac\pi4\right)=\dfrac{\sqrt2\pi^2}{16}\), \(y\left(\frac\pi3\right)=\dfrac{2\pi^2}9\), \(y'\left(\frac\pi3\right)=\dfrac{4\pi}3+\dfrac{2\sqrt3\pi^2}9\).

questions.q: Let \(y(x)\) be a solution of the differential equation \((1+e^x)y'+ye^x=1\). If \(y(0)=2\), then which of the following statements is (are) true?
opts: \(y(x)\) has a critical point in the interval \((-1,0)\)
\(y(x)\) has no critical point in the interval \((-1,0)\)
questions.sol: \(\left(y(1+e^x)\right)'=1\) gives \(y=\dfrac{x+4}{1+e^x}\). \(y'=0\) when \(e^x(x+3)=1\); \(e^x(x+3)-1\) is negative at \(-1\) and positive at \(0\).

questions.q: Consider the family of all circles whose centres lie on the straight line \(y=x\). If this family of circles is represented by the differential equation \(Py''+Qy'+1=0\), where \(P,Q\) are functions of \(x,y\) and \(y'\) (here \(y'=\dfrac{dy}{dx}\), \(y''=\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\)), then which of the following statements is (are) true?
Let \(f:(0,\infty)\to R\) be a differentiable function such that \(f'(x)=2-\dfrac{f(x)}x\) for all \(x\in(0,\infty)\) and \(f(1)\ne1\). Then
questions.sol: \((xf)'=2x\) gives \(f=x+\dfrac cx\) with \(c\ne0\). \(f'\left(\frac1x\right)=1-cx^2\to1\); \(xf\left(\frac1x\right)\to1\); \(x^2f'(x)\to-c\ne0\); \(f\) is unbounded near \(0\).

questions.q: A solution curve of the differential equation \((x^2+xy+4x+2y+4)\dfrac{dy}{dx}-y^2=0\), \(x>0\) passes through the point \((1,3)\). Then the solution curve
questions.sol: The bracket is \((x+2)(x+2+y)\). With \(X=x+2\), \(y=vX\): \(\dfrac{1+v}vdv=-\dfrac{dX}X\), so \(\ln y+\dfrac y{x+2}=\ln3+1\). On \(y=x+2\): \(\ln(x+2)=\ln3\), only \(x=1\). On \(y=(x+2)^2\) or \((x+3)^2\) with \(x>0\) the left side exceeds \(\ln3+1\): no intersection.

questions.q: Let \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) and \(g:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be two non-constant differentiable functions. If \(f'(x)=\left(e^{(f(x)-g(x))}\right)g'(x)\) for all \(x\in\mathbb R\), and \(f(1)=g(2)=1\), then which of the following statement(s) is (are) TRUE?
questions.sol: \(e^{-f}f'=e^{-g}g'\) gives \(e^{-f}-e^{-g}=\) constant. Using \(x=1\) and \(x=2\): \(e^{-f(2)}+e^{-g(1)}=\dfrac2e\). Each term is positive, so each is less than \(\dfrac2e\): \(f(2)>1-\ln2\) and \(g(1)>1-\ln2\).

questions.q: Let \(f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\) be a continuous function such that \(f(x)=1-2x+\displaystyle\int_0^xe^{x-t}f(t)dt\) for all \(x\in[0,\infty)\). Then, which of the following statement(s) is (are) TRUE?
opts: The curve \(y=f(x)\) passes through the point \((1,2)\)
The curve \(y=f(x)\) passes through the point \((2,-1)\)
The area of the region \(\{(x,y)\in[0,1]\times\mathbb R:f(x)\le y\le\sqrt{1-x^2}\}\) is \(\dfrac{\pi-2}4\)
The area of the region \(\{(x,y)\in[0,1]\times\mathbb R:f(x)\le y\le\sqrt{1-x^2}\}\) is \(\dfrac{\pi-1}4\)
questions.sol: Multiplying by \(e^{-x}\) and differentiating: \(f'-2f=2x-3\) with \(f(0)=1\), whose solution is \(f=1-x\). The region is a quarter disc minus a triangle: \(\dfrac\pi4-\dfrac12\).

questions.q: Let \(\Gamma\) denote a curve \(y=y(x)\) which is in the first quadrant and let the point \((1,0)\) lies on it. Let the tangent to \(\Gamma\) at a point \(P\) intersect the \(y\)-axis at \(Y_P\). If \(PY_P\) has length \(1\) for each point \(P\) on \(\Gamma\), then which of the following options is/are correct?
questions.sol: \(Y_P=(0,y-xy')\), so \(x^2+x^2y'^2=1\) and \(y'=\pm\dfrac{\sqrt{1-x^2}}x\). The curve is above the axis and reaches \(0\) at \(x=1\), so it is decreasing: \(xy'+\sqrt{1-x^2}=0\). Integrating with \(y(1)=0\): \(y=\log_e\dfrac{1+\sqrt{1-x^2}}x-\sqrt{1-x^2}\).

questions.q: For any real numbers \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\), let \(y_{\alpha,\beta}(x)\), \(x\in\mathbb R\), be the solution of the differential equation \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\alpha y=xe^{\beta x}\), \(y(1)=1\). Let \(S=\{y_{\alpha,\beta}(x):\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb R\}\). Then which of the following functions belong(s) to the set \(S\)?
questions.sol: If \(\alpha+\beta=0\): \(y=\left(\dfrac{x^2}2+C\right)e^{-\alpha x}\); (a) is this with \(\alpha=1\), \(C=e-\dfrac12\), while (b) has the wrong sign of \(x^2\). If \(\alpha+\beta\ne0\): \(y=e^{\beta x}\left(\dfrac x{\alpha+\beta}-\dfrac1{(\alpha+\beta)^2}\right)+Ce^{-\alpha x}\); (c) is this with \(\alpha=\beta=1\) and \(y(1)=1\); (d) would need \(\alpha+\beta=-2\) with \(\beta=1\), but then the last term would be \(e^{3x}\).

questions.q: For \(x\in R\), let the function \(y(x)\) be the solution of the differential equation \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}+12y=\cos\left(\dfrac\pi{12}x\right)\), \(y(0)=0\). Then, which of the following statements is/are true?
opts: There exists a real number \(\beta\) such that the line \(y=\beta\) intersects the curve \(y=y(x)\) at infinitely many points
questions.sol: \(y=A\cos\dfrac{\pi x}{12}+B\sin\dfrac{\pi x}{12}-Ae^{-12x}\) with \(A>0\). The oscillating part makes \(y\) neither increasing nor decreasing, the term \(e^{-12x}\) destroys periodicity, and for large \(x\) the curve keeps crossing a line such as \(y=0\).

questions.q: If \((a+bx)e^{y/x}=x\) then prove that \(x^3\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=\left(x\dfrac{dy}{dx}-y\right)^2\)
questions.sol: \(\dfrac yx=\ln x-\ln(a+bx)\). Differentiating: \(\dfrac{xy'-y}{x^2}=\dfrac a{x(a+bx)}\), i.e. \(xy'-y=\dfrac{ax}{a+bx}\). Differentiating again: \(xy''=\dfrac{a^2}{(a+bx)^2}\), so \(x^3y''=\left(\dfrac{ax}{a+bx}\right)^2\).

questions.q: If \(x=\sec\theta-\cos\theta\) and \(y=\sec^n\theta-\cos^n\theta\), then show that \((x^2+4)\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2=n^2(y^2+4)\)
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{dx}{d\theta}=\tan\theta(\sec\theta+\cos\theta)\), \(\dfrac{dy}{d\theta}=n\tan\theta(\sec^n\theta+\cos^n\theta)\). Also \(x^2+4=(\sec\theta+\cos\theta)^2\) and \(y^2+4=(\sec^n\theta+\cos^n\theta)^2\).

questions.q: A normal is drawn at a point \(P(x,y)\) of a curve meets the \(x\)-axis at \(Q\). If \(PQ\) is of constant length \(K\), then show that the differential equation of the curve is \(y\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\pm\sqrt{K^2-y^2}\).
questions.sol: The length of the normal is \(y\sqrt{1+y'^2}=K\), so \(y^2y'^2=K^2-y^2\).

questions.q: Let \(y=f(x)\) be a curve passing through \((1,1)\) such that the triangle formed by the coordinate axes and the tangent at any point of the curve lies in the \(1^{st}\) quadrant and has area \(2\). Form the differential equations and determine all such possible curves.
questions.sol: Intercepts \(x-\dfrac y{y'}\) and \(y-xy'\): \(\dfrac{(y-xy')^2}{-2y'}=2\), i.e. \(y=xp+2\sqrt{-p}\) \((p=y')\), a Clairaut equation. General solution \(y=cx+2\sqrt{-c}\); through \((1,1)\): \(c=-1\), giving \(x+y=2\). Singular solution: \(x=\dfrac1{\sqrt{-p}}\), giving \(xy=1\).

questions.q: Determine the equation of the curve passing through the origin, in the form \(y=f(x)\), which satisfies the differential equation \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\sin(10x+6y)\).
questions.sol: With \(t=10x+6y\): \(\dfrac{dt}{10+6\sin t}=dx\); putting \(u=\tan\dfrac t2\): \(\dfrac14\tan^{-1}\dfrac{5u+3}4=x+\dfrac14\tan^{-1}\dfrac34\). So \(\dfrac{5u+3}4=\dfrac{4\tan4x+3}{4-3\tan4x}\), giving \(u=\tan(5x+3y)=\dfrac{5\tan4x}{4-3\tan4x}\).

questions.q: Let \(u(x)\) and \(v(x)\) satisfy the differential equations \(\dfrac{du}{dx}+P(x)u=f(x)\) and \(\dfrac{dv}{dx}+P(x)v=g(x)\), where \(P(x)\), \(f(x)\) and \(g(x)\) are continuous functions. If \(u(x_1)>v(x_1)\) for some \(x_1\) and \(f(x)>g(x)\) for all \(x>x_1\), prove that any point \((x,y)\) where \(x>x_1\) does not satisfy the equations \(y=u(x)\) and \(y=v(x)\).
questions.sol: \(w=u-v\) satisfies \(w'+Pw=f-g>0\) for \(x>x_1\), so \(\left(we^{\int P\,dx}\right)'>0\): \(we^{\int P}\) is increasing and positive at \(x_1\). Hence \(u(x)>v(x)\) for all \(x>x_1\), and the two curves have no common point there.

questions.q: A curve passing through the point \((1,1)\) has the property that the perpendicular distance of the origin from the normal at any point \(P\) of the curve is equal to the distance of \(P\) from the axis. Determine the equation of the curve.
questions.sol: Normal: \(X+y'Y=x+yy'\). \(\dfrac{|x+yy'|}{\sqrt{1+y'^2}}=|y|\) gives \(x^2+2xyy'=y^2\). With \(w=y^2\): \(\left(\dfrac wx\right)'=-1\), so \(y^2=-x^2+cx\) and \(c=2\).

questions.q: A curve passes through \((2,0)\) and slope at point \(P(x,y)\) is \(\dfrac{(x+1)^2+(y-3)}{(x+1)}\). Find equation of curve and area between curve and \(x\)-axis in \(4^{th}\) quadrant.
questions.sol: With \(X=x+1\), \(Y=y-3\): \(\left(\dfrac YX\right)'=1\), so \(Y=X^2+cX\); \((2,0)\) gives \(c=-4\): \(y=x^2-2x\). Area \(=\displaystyle\int_0^2(2x-x^2)dx\).

questions.q: A spherical rain drop evaporates at a rate proportional to its surface area at any instant \(t\). The differential equation giving the rate of change of the radius of the rain drop is ..........
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{dV}{dt}=-K(4\pi r^2)\) and \(\dfrac{dV}{dt}=4\pi r^2\dfrac{dr}{dt}\).

questions.q:
Column IColumn II
(i) \(\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}(\sin x)^{\cos x}\left(\cos x\cot x-\log(\sin x)^{\sin x}\right)dx\)(A) \(1\)
(ii) Area bounded by \(-4y^2=x\) and \(x-1=-5y^2\)(B) \(0\)
(iii) Cosine of the angle of intersection of curves \(y=3^{x-1}\log x\) and \(y=x^x-1\) is(C) \(Ke^{y/2}\)
(iv) Solution of differential equation \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac2{(x+y)}\) is \(x+y+2=\) ........(D) \(4/3\)
questions.sol: (i) The integrand is the derivative of \((\sin x)^{\cos x}\): \(1-0\). (ii) The curves meet at \(y=\pm1\): \(\displaystyle\int_{-1}^1(1-y^2)dy=\dfrac43\). (iii) They meet at \(x=1\) and both have slope \(1\) there: angle \(0\), cosine \(1\). (iv) With \(t=x+y\): \(\dfrac{t\,dt}{t+2}=dx\) gives \(y-2\ln(x+y+2)=c\). (The book key prints (iii) \(\to\) (B).)

questions.q:
Let a solution \(y=y(x)\) of the differential equation \(x\sqrt{x^2-1}\,dy-y\sqrt{y^2-1}\,dx=0\) satisfies \(y(2)=\dfrac2{\sqrt3}\).
Statement - 1 : \(y(x)=\sec\left(\sec^{-1}x-\dfrac\pi6\right)\)
Statement - 2 : \(y(x)\) is given by \(\dfrac1y=\dfrac{2\sqrt3}x-\sqrt{1-\dfrac1{x^2}}\)
opts: Statement-1 is True, Statement-2 is True; Statement-2 is a correct explanation of Statement-1
Statement-1 is True, Statement-2 is True; Statement-2 is NOT a correct explanation for Statement-1
Statement-1 is True, Statement-2 is False
Statement-1 is False, Statement-2 is True.
questions.sol: \(\sec^{-1}y=\sec^{-1}x+c\) and \(\dfrac\pi6=\dfrac\pi3+c\): Statement-1 is true. Then \(\dfrac1y=\cos\left(\sec^{-1}x-\dfrac\pi6\right)=\dfrac{\sqrt3}{2x}+\dfrac12\sqrt{1-\dfrac1{x^2}}\), so Statement-2 is false.

questions.q: Let \(f\) be a real-valued differentiable function on \(R\) (the set of all real numbers) such that \(f(1)=1\). If the \(y\)-intercept of the tangent at any point \(P(x,y)\) on the curve \(y=f(x)\) is equal to the cube of the abscissa of \(P\), then the value of \(f(-3)\) is equal to ______
questions.sol: \(y-xy'=x^3\), i.e. \(\left(\dfrac yx\right)'=-x\): \(y=-\dfrac{x^3}2+\dfrac{3x}2\). \(f(-3)=\dfrac{27}2-\dfrac92=9\). (The book key prints \(1\).)

questions.q: Let \(f:[1,\infty)\to[2,\infty)\) be a differentiable function such that \(f(1)=2\). If \(6\displaystyle\int_1^xf(t)dt=3xf(x)-x^3\) for all \(x\ge1\), then the value of \(f(2)\) is
questions.sol: Differentiating: \(6f=3f+3xf'-3x^2\), i.e. \(\left(\dfrac fx\right)'=1\), so \(f=x^2+cx\) and \(f(1)=2\) gives \(c=1\): \(f(2)=6\). (At \(x=1\) the given relation itself is not satisfied — a known flaw in the question; the intended answer is \(6\).)

questions.q: Let \(y'(x)+y(x)g'(x)=g(x)g'(x)\), \(y(0)=0\), \(x\in R\), where \(f'(x)\) denotes \(\dfrac{df(x)}{dx}\) and \(g(x)\) is a given non-constant differentiable function on \(R\) with \(g(0)=g(2)=0\). Then the value of \(y(2)\) is

Let \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be a differentiable function with \(f(0)=0\). If \(y=f(x)\) satisfies the differential equation \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=(2+5y)(5y-2)\), then the value of \(\lim\limits_{x\to-\infty}f(x)\) is _____ .
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{dy}{25y^2-4}=dx\) gives \(\dfrac{5y-2}{5y+2}=-e^{20x}\) (using \(y(0)=0\)). As \(x\to-\infty\) the right side tends to \(0\): \(y\to\dfrac25\).

questions.q: Let \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be a differentiable function with \(f(0)=1\) and satisfying the equation \(f(x+y)=f(x)f'(y)+f'(x)f(y)\) for all \(x,y\in\mathbb R\). Then, the value of \(\log_e(f(4))\) is ____ .

If \(y(x)\) is the solution of the differential equation \(x\,dy-(y^2-4y)dx=0\) for \(x>0\), \(y(1)=2\), and the slope of the curve \(y=y(x)\) is never zero, then the value of \(10y(\sqrt2)\) is _____
questions.sol: \(\dfrac{dy}{y(y-4)}=\dfrac{dx}x\) gives \(\dfrac{4-y}y=x^4\) (constant fixed by \(y(1)=2\)), so \(y=\dfrac4{1+x^4}\) and \(y(\sqrt2)=\dfrac45\).

questions.q: For \(x\in\mathbb R\), let \(y(x)\) be a solution of the differential equation \((x^2-5)\dfrac{dy}{dx}-2xy=-2x(x^2-5)^2\) such that \(y(2)=7\). Then the maximum value of the function \(y(x)\) is
Let \(y(x)\) be the solution of the differential equation \(x^2\dfrac{dy}{dx}+xy=x^2+y^2\), \(x>\dfrac1e\), satisfying \(y(1)=0\). Then the value of \(2\dfrac{(y(e))^2}{y(e^2)}\) is ______.
questions.sol: With \(y=vx\): \(x\dfrac{dv}{dx}=(v-1)^2\), so \(\dfrac1{1-v}=\ln x+1\) and \(y=\dfrac{x\ln x}{1+\ln x}\). \(y(e)=\dfrac e2\), \(y(e^2)=\dfrac{2e^2}3\): value \(\dfrac34\).

questions.q: Let \(y:(-\infty,\infty)\to(0,\infty)\) be the solution of the differential equation \(\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{e^{5x}y^3+y^3}{e^x+e^xy^4}\), satisfying \(y(0)=\dfrac1{\sqrt2}\). Then the value of \(y(\log_e2)\) is

Let \(y=f(x)\) be the real valued function defined on the interval \((0,\infty)\), satisfying \(y(1)=0\) and the differential equation \(x\dfrac{dy}{dx}=y-x^3\).
Then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE ?
opts: The function \(f\) has a local minimum at \(x=\dfrac1{\sqrt3}\)
The function \(f\) has a local maximum at \(x=\dfrac1{\sqrt3}\)
The function \(f\) is increasing in the interval \((1,2)\)
If \(g(x)=4x^3-5x^2+\dfrac32x\) for \(x>0\), then the number of elements in the set \(\{x\in(0,\infty):f(x)=g(x)\}\) is \(2\)
questions.sol: \(\left(\dfrac yx\right)'=-x\) and \(y(1)=0\): \(f(x)=\dfrac{x-x^3}2\). \(f'=\dfrac{1-3x^2}2\) changes from \(+\) to \(-\) at \(\dfrac1{\sqrt3}\) and is negative on \((1,2)\). \(f=g\): \(x(9x^2-10x+2)=0\), with two positive roots.
